catalog_quote: § 7. ACCENT.—The general rule is: the accent lies on the penult, provided this does not contain ĕ (medio-palatal, French 'e muet'):— kápa', hatchet. dinándu, woman. nusáï, what? kasábay, arrived. Bolongan { tĕráŋ (voc. t'ráng), clear. kĕpá', curtailed. gĕnáp (voc. g'nap), enough, complete. In Tarakan instances of ĕ in the penult are extremely rare: mĕñjul, through (voc. m'njul). § 8. It is sometimes difficult to make out which syllable is the penult, when a word is not heard. Suffixes may cause a shift of accent to the new penult, the suffix being felt as part of the word to which it has been added, but only if the word ends in a vowel: in nusáï (compound of nu + sa + i) i is a suffix; in bálay, house (voc. balei), there is none; in tĕtápi, but, there is no suffix; in naŋkúbi, to cover (from táŋkup), there is; in pupus-nia, afterwards, the original accent remains; in sāmá-mu ñandāgu, don't speak, mu is a suffix; in cōbé-m pānaw, do go away now (Bolongan), the m corresponds to the same -mu (you). N.B.—nia in Tar. and na in Bol., both meaning 'already' and denoting a sort of affirmation like Malay lah, are no suffixes. They ought therefore to be written separately, and so ought lah in Malay. ... They are enclitic particles indeed, [Fokker, Appendix, p. 109] | [Beech, p. 19] For the pronunciation of words a general rule can be made that the accent falls on the penultimate, as in Malay, Dayak, Javanese, Sundanese, &c.

ACCENT.—The general rule is : the accent lies on the penult, provided this does not contain ĕ (medio-palatal, French ' e muet ') :— kápa', hatchet. dinándu, woman. nusái, what ? kasábay, arrived. Bolongan { tĕráŋ (voc. t'ráng), clear. kĕpá', curtailed. gĕnáp (voc. g'nap), enough, complete. In Tarakan instances of ĕ in the penult are extremely rare : mĕnjul, through (voc. m'njul)." and §8: "Suffixes may cause a shift of accent to the new penult, the suffix being felt as…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; if the penult vowel is schwa (ĕ) the accent goes to the final syllable instead (schwa penults are rare in Tarakan Tidung, commoner in Bolongan). Suffixation moves the accent to the new penult when the stem is vowel-final; enclitic particles do not.
new_statements.exceptions: Penults containing ĕ (schwa) do not take the accent (examples stressed on the final: tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp; Tarakan mĕnjúl) — such penults are 'extremely rare' in Tarakan. Suffixes shift accent to the new penult only when the stem ends in a vowel (nusái, naŋkúbi); in pupus-nia the original accent remains; p. 60 footnote: pa-bási 'pa being only a causative prefix, the accent falls on the second syllable'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the rule is stated for words (pronunciation of vocabulary items) and for suffixed words; §8 adds that enclitic particles (Tar. nia, Bol. na 'already') are not suffixes and do not shift the accent, so the domain is the morphological word including suffixes but excluding enclitics.
new_statements.identity_note: Beech 1908 describes two 'Tidong dialects': Tarakan (Tarakan Island, North Kalimantan = Southern Tidung, sout3241) and Bolongan (= Bulungan, a separate Glottolog language bolo1268; Glottolog cites Beech 1908 for both). Beech's p. 19 rule is stated for both dialects; Fokker's §7 gives four Tarakan examples plus three Bolongan schwa-penult examples and notes schwa penults are 'extremely rare' in Tarakan. The other opened sources cover Sebatik/Sabah Tidung (Mahali 2019, likely nort3262/itd border area) and Nunukan Tidung (Aqromi & Hendrawan 2018), none with a stress statement.
